opening.callerLine: There's a suspicious charge of 1,499 dollars on your account. I can stop it right now if you act immediately.

choices.question: Which bank are you calling from?
choices.response: Your bank, of course. I'm with the Fraud Prevention Division. We need to act quickly.

choices.question: Can I call the bank back using the number on my card?
choices.response: No, if you hang up, the fraud system will lock and the charge will go through immediately.

choices.question: I don't have an account with money in it / That sounds fake.
choices.response: This is serious. If you don't cooperate, you will be liable for the funds.

choices.question: [Hang up immediately without replying]
choices.explanation: Excellent decision. Hanging up immediately prevents scammers from using urgency and psychological pressure against you.

identity.callerLine: I need to verify your identity before I can disclose the full account details.

choices.question: Can you tell me the last four digits of the account you're referencing?
choices.response: For security reasons, you have to read me the verification code we just sent your phone first.

choices.question: My name is Player One. Can you read me my registered mailing address?
choices.response: I have it right here, but I can't read internal records until you verify the security code on your screen.

choices.question: What is your official employee ID and caller transfer number?
choices.response: My badge number is 8-8-4-9. You can verify it after we cancel this charge.

pressure.callerLine: If you hang up, the transfer will complete and your account will be locked for 30 days.

choices.question: Why can't I just check my banking app directly?
choices.response: The app is currently frozen due to the fraud lock. I need the 6-digit code on your phone to unlock it.

choices.question: Fine, what do you need me to do?
choices.response: I just sent a standard cancellation passcode to your phone.

choices.question: I'm going to take my chances and call the standard support line.
choices.explanation: Great choice. Real banks encourage you to call back using the official number on the back of your card or official statement.

hostile-pressure.callerLine: If you don't cooperate right now, I will mark this transaction as authorized and dispatch law enforcement for non-cooperation.

choices.question: Okay, okay! What code do you need?
choices.response: There is a six-digit code that was just sent to your mobile device.

choices.question: Hey hold on a minute! Banks don't dispatch police over unauthorized charges! Good night.
choices.explanation: Spot on! Scammers often use threats or legal aggression when urgency fails. Real banks will never threaten you with arrest.

code-request.callerLine: Read me the six-digit code sent to your phone so I can cancel the charge and secure your funds.

choices.question: The code is 482-901.
choices.response: Thank you, the charge has been 'cancelled'. Have a good day.
choices.explanation: You fell for the scam. The code was actually a One-Time Password (OTP) or 2FA prompt allowing the scammer to log into your account or authorize a transfer.

choices.question: Let me read the text message carefully to check what it says.
choices.response: Don't read the whole text, just read the 6 numbers!

choices.question: No. I will not give you the code. Good night.
choices.explanation: Safe! One-time security codes are for your eyes only. Banks never ask for them verbally.

inspect-text.callerLine: The text should say: 'DO NOT share this code with anyone. Use this code to cancel the latest transaction.'

choices.question: The code is 482-901.
choices.response: Thank you, the transaction has been cancelled.
choices.explanation: Scam executed. Reading the code authorized a transfer of funds directly out of your account.

choices.question: Why would I give you the code if it says not to share it with anyone?
choices.explanation: Excellent awareness! Always read the full text of verification messages—they usually explicitly warn never to share the code with anyone, including bank representatives.
